picks.intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform, NCT03326921)
picks.rationale: She came to Libby for HLA-restricted immunotherapy, and three of the four HA-directed products shut the door on prior allo-HCT. NCT03326921 does the opposite: a prior graft is an entry requirement rather than an exclusion, there is no marrow-blast ceiling and no performance-status floor, and 4 of 9 infused patients achieved or held a CR with no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS (pmid:38683966). Nothing in her preference file blocks this, since toxicity_vetoes and modality_constraints are both empty and travel to a single Seattle site is acceptable under prefers_trials with geography_band null. What blocks it is a records request and two genotypes, and the FHCC intake line (206-606-4668, immunotherapy@fredhutch.org) can be asked whether they run the HA-1 rs1801284 typing on her and the sibling during screening.
primary_concerns: Two gates are still unopened and either one can close this permanently: she must be HLA-A*02:01 positive and HA-1(H) positive (rs1801284 A/G or A/A) with a sibling who is HA-1(H)-negative or A*02:01-negative.
n=9 on a feasibility endpoint. Nobody should hear 4 of 9 as a response rate, and I would say that to her in those words.
The product is made from donor cells, so the sibling has to agree to a fresh collection before anything gets manufactured. That consent conversation is on the critical path and nobody has started it.

A relapse six years out is exactly where HLA class II downregulation and antigen-presentation escape turn up (pmid:30380364). Germline A*02:01 positivity does not prove the relapsed clone still presents it, which is why the HLA-LOH read on sorted blasts belongs in the same workup.

Preference axes fully satisfied: prefers_trials, travel, empty vetoes, empty modality constraints, curative intent. In tension: nothing, until organ function is documented and the 0.75 efficacy weight gets the revisit her own free text asks for.

picks.intervention_label: CBX-250, CG1/HLA-A*02:01 x CD3 TCR-mimetic bispecific engager (CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676)
picks.rationale: If the HA-1 genotypes do not line up, this is the other half of the same records request, because CBX-250 rides HLA-A*02:01 alone and asks nothing of the sibling. The protocol calls relapse at any time after HSCT eligible, ECOG 0-1 matches her, eleven US sites beat one, and Crossbow publishes a compassionate-use address (clinical@crossbowtx.com) for a patient who cannot get a slot, which almost nothing else in this dossier offers. There is no human efficacy number yet; the case rests on an engager that killed HLA-A2-positive primary AML in vitro and in vivo and left normal marrow alone (pmid:39939820, pmid:40437170). Her file vetoes no toxicity, so cytokine release is a conversation to have with her rather than a reason I would strike this off her list.
primary_concerns: Phase 1 dose escalation with no efficacy readout in humans. I am ranking this on eligibility fit and reachability, not on evidence, and she should hear it framed that way.
WBC has to be under 25,000 at enrollment against peripheral blasts that ran 58 to 82 percent, so this only becomes real after cytoreduction (pick 3).

Same master switch as pick 1. If the 2020 report comes back A*02:01-negative, picks 1 and 2 both close on the same afternoon, and the A*24:02 line in that report is then the only HLA-restricted thread left worth pulling.
Worth asking the sponsor whether CG1 expression is measured on study or whether A*02:01 alone qualifies, so the workup list is complete before anyone books a flight.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO: cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin (NCT04050280)
picks.rationale: Everything above needs her blast burden down first. CBX-250 wants a white count under 25,000, sibling DLI protocols cap blasts at 30 percent, and a payer will want documented disease control before authorising a second graft, so cytoreduction is what makes the immunotherapy goal reachable rather than a detour away from it. NCT04050280 names post-allograft relapse as eligible at 60 days or more off immunosuppression with no more than grade 1 GVHD, and if the Baltimore slot does not open the regimen can be rebuilt from marketed drugs at her home centre, which is a fallback almost nothing else here has. Two honest caveats she is entitled to: fractionated gemtuzumab monotherapy produced 26% CR in first relapse rather than refractory disease (pmid:17051246), and in the 3,325-patient individual-patient-data meta-analysis the adverse-cytogenetics group saw no survival benefit from gemtuzumab (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18, p=0.9; pmid:25008258), which is her karyotype.
primary_concerns: The efficacy weight of 0.75 argues for an intensive cytoreduction, but her free text says that number was set before anyone documented her fitness. Cardiac and hepatic assessment first, then re-check this pick against it. I am not comfortable ranking a cladribine/cytarabine backbone as if organ function were known when it is not.

The adverse-karyotype meta-analysis result is the real weakness here and I would rather put it in front of her than bury it. Quantitative CD33 density and rs12459419 genotype would at least tell her how much to expect.

Marrow-derived CD33 does not speak for the thigh sarcoma. Paired myeloid sarcoma series show CD33 detectable in 79 percent of lesions rather than all, so the extramedullary site may not answer to a CD33-directed regimen even if the marrow does.
This is a bridge, not a destination. If nobody has planned the cellular or transplant consolidation before it starts, a response gets spent rather than used.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) from the HLA-identical sibling, sequential cytoreduction into reduced-intensity conditioning
picks.rationale: This is the honest answer to a stated curative intent, and it is the platform the HLA-restricted consolidation in picks 1 and 2 is supposed to sit on top of. Her stratum is the favourable one on nearly every axis the registries measure: a related-donor first transplant carries 37% +/- 6% two-year survival versus 16% +/- 4% after an unrelated one (pmid:23918951), and a six-year remission sits far past the five-month cut that drives the EBMT prognostic score (pmid:22167752). The exception is the one that matters most today, roughly 85% marrow blasts, which is why I rank this under the cytoreduction rather than over it; DLI given with active disease runs 15% +/- 3% two-year survival against 56% +/- 10% given in remission (pmid:17909197). No preference blocks it, since HCT2 is named as acceptable and no modality is ruled out, but fitness for a second conditioning regimen is undocumented and that assessment should be booked this week rather than after the workup returns.
primary_concerns: Fitness is the load-bearing unknown. Her preference file explicitly asks for the 0.75 efficacy weight to be revisited once organ function is documented, and a second allograft is the pick where that revisit changes the answer most.
The US sequential-conditioning route (NCT06928662) repeats a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through. That is a clinical objection to raise with the investigator, not an access one.

Donor questions nobody has closed: germline predisposition shared with the sibling would redirect donor choice, and the hereditary panel needs cultured fibroblasts rather than blood while blasts are circulating.
Payer authorisation is likelier to turn on documented cytoreduction than on anything biological, which is another reason pick 3 precedes this one.

picks.intervention_label: BMS-986497 (ORM-6151), CD33-directed antibody-conjugated GSPT1 degrader, monotherapy arm (NCT06419634)
picks.rationale: A trial fallback that does not depend on the HLA answer at all, which matters because picks 1 and 2 stand or fall on one allele. CD33 only has to be detectable rather than above a threshold, MDS-related secondary AML is named in the inclusion criteria, and the posted criteria carry no blast cap and no bar on a prior allograft, which is rare across the 47 trials screened here. Push for the monotherapy arm rather than the azacitidine-venetoclax triplet, since she progressed through venetoclax and re-exposing her to it would spend a trial slot on a drug she has already failed. First in human, so there is no efficacy figure to quote, and the absent exclusions should be confirmed with the site before she travels.
primary_concerns: No published clinical data of any kind. This is on the list because it is open, reachable and compatible with prefers_trials, not because anyone knows what it does.
Trial-arm assignment may not be hers to choose. If the site will only take her onto the triplet, the venetoclax objection stands and I would rather she kept the slot for something else.
Enrolling here consumes weeks that an 85% marrow may not have, so it competes with pick 3 on time rather than complementing it.

notes: Two things I do not want the board to let slide. First, the A*24:02 branch: profile.json says both alleles have to be resolved before HLA-restricted immunotherapy is written off, and the same 2020 typing report answers both, so whoever pulls it should transcribe the whole class I result rather than just the A*02 line. That said, I did not rank the WT1-siTCR route, because the accessibility read is Japan-only with no enrolling study a US patient can enter, and telling her that a door is open when the sponsor is not opening it would be worse than telling her it is shut. Second, the efficacy weight. She set 0.75 before anyone documented her organ function and her own free text asks for it to be revisited once fitness is known; I have ranked as if 0.75 holds, and picks 3 and 4 are the ones that would move if a cardiac or hepatic assessment came back poor. What I keep coming back to is that the highest-yield action in this entire dossier is a phone call to the 2020 transplant centre asking for an allele-level report that already exists. She asked for HLA-restricted immunotherapy. The flagship products (NCT05473910, NCT06704152) exclude her prior allograft and that is a real narrowing, but NCT03326921 requires it and NCT06994676 accepts it, so the pathway is narrower than she hoped rather than closed, and it is still gated on a value sitting unretrieved in a chart.

picks.intervention_label: Gating workup before any therapeutic commitment: fitness and organ-function documentation (CrCl, LFTs including bilirubin, ejection fraction) plus HLA class I typing, HA-1/HA-2 genotyping of patient and sibling donor, quantitative CD33/CD123 antigen density, and TP53 variant-level NGS with copy-number calling
picks.rationale: Nothing below this line can be priced without labs that do not exist yet. There is no creatinine clearance, no LFTs and no cardiac study in the record, and profile.json calls the fitness assessment an explicit open item, which means every toxicity claim any of us makes this round is unanchored. The same visit buys the assays the rest of the board is arguing over, and two of those gates are hard numbers a screening coordinator will apply: CLAG-GO on NCT04050280 needs CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, and the tagraxofusp cohort on NCT03113643 needs albumin above 3.2 g/dL. preferences.json says the 0.75 efficacy weight should be revisited once fitness is known, and I read that as the patient asking for exactly this step.
primary_concerns: Delay is itself a harm here. Peripheral blasts went 58% to 82% inside a fortnight, so this workup runs alongside starting cytoreduction, not before it.

HA-1 genotyping at rs1801284 is not a routine US send-out. The Fred Hutch screening pathway on NCT03326921 may be the fastest route to a result for both her and the sibling, which makes this a referral clock rather than a lab clock.
A tidy chemistry panel from one draw is not a cardiac assessment. I want a measured ejection fraction on the chart before anyone writes idarubicin or a second conditioning regimen.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO: cladribine, high-dose cytarabine and G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 (NCT04050280)
picks.rationale: Fractionated gemtuzumab is the one cytoreductive component here whose safety record survives contact with a patient heading for another graft: Taksin's 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 produced no grade 3-4 hepatic toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease in 57 patients, seven of whom were transplanted afterwards, and Hills found fewer early deaths at 3 mg/m2 than at 6 mg/m2 for the same efficacy. The expectation has to be set honestly against the same evidence base: in adverse cytogenetics the 6-year survival benefit was OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18), p=0.9, and ALFA-0701 enrolled de novo AML only, so neither trial says her MDS-related complex-karyotype disease will respond. I would run it through NCT04050280 rather than as off-label dosing, because that protocol was written for this exact situation, refractory after intensive therapy with a prior allograft permitted at 60 days or more provided GVHD is grade 1 at most. Entry turns on CD33 on at least 20% of blasts, which the qualitative flow result does not establish.
primary_concerns: Adverse karyotype is precisely where the CD33 evidence is weakest. OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18) is not a signal and I will not let it be sold as one.

Fractionation lowers veno-occlusive risk, it does not zero it, and the whole plan points at another conditioning regimen within months of the last dose. Baseline bilirubin and transaminases before dose one, then weekly.
Cladribine plus high-dose cytarabine on a graft that has been in place six years. Count recovery may be slow, and the step after this one needs a countable remission rather than an aplastic marrow.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT from the HLA-identical sibling, with sequential cytoreductive conditioning (e.g. DEC-FLAG-Ida/RIC, NCT06928662), performed only after documented cytoreduction
picks.rationale: A sibling graft is the only thing in this dossier with a documented cure fraction, and her stratum in Christopeit's registry, a related-donor first transplant, sat at 2-year OS 37% +/- 6%. Almost every favourable factor in Ruutu's 2632-patient EBMT series is hers as well, a six-year first remission, a long intertransplant interval and a sibling donor, with one exception, and that exception is 85% marrow blasts. Schmid's post-RIC-relapse score puts the worst band at 4% +/- 2% at two years and gives blasts below 27% an HR of 0.53, so taking her to conditioning with the marrow as it stands spends the non-relapse mortality without buying the survival. I support HCT2 as the destination and I would gate it on a documented remission or at least blasts under 27%, a measured ejection fraction, and a creatinine clearance.
primary_concerns: Non-relapse mortality is the number nobody actually has for her. All three registry rows report survival and none tabulates adverse events, so the tolerability case rests on curves rather than a per-organ risk table.
Conditioning intensity is unresolved and there is no cardiac or renal baseline from which to choose it. That decision should not be made on an ECOG score alone.

A second graft from the same sibling does nothing about whatever let this leukaemia escape graft-versus-leukaemia the first time. The class II downregulation and HLA-loss rows in the preclinical set are a reason to check for HLA loss on the blasts before assuming the donor is the answer.

picks.intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion (Bleakley platform, NCT03326921), as post-graft consolidation
picks.rationale: This is the best-tolerated product in the dossier and I do not say that lightly about a phase 1 with nine patients: no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS, with the two mild acute GVHD cases attributed to immunosuppression withdrawal before infusion rather than to the cells. Four of nine achieved or maintained CR and one has been MRD-negative beyond 27 months, which is worth chasing, though the denominator is 9 and the trial was never powered to say so. It is also the only HA-1 programme that requires a prior allograft instead of excluding one, which is why TSC-100/101 and BSB-1001 are shut to her and this is not. What it cannot do is clear 85% blasts, since grade 3-5 infections followed the lymphodepletion in this series and the MDG1011 investigators attributed their own phase 1 failure to tumour burden, so I would place it after cytoreduction and after the graft rather than instead of either.
primary_concerns: Nine infused patients is not a safety database. The specific missing datum is the one that matters most here: the report describes no patient infused after a second allograft, so the interaction with HCT2 immunosuppression and engraftment is unmeasured rather than reassuring.
Both gates are shut until typing returns. A*02:01 plus the directional HA-1 mismatch, recipient A/G or A/A with donor G/G, and nobody has genotyped either of them.

One grade 4 infusion reaction in 9, and grade 3-5 infections after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide. Lymphodepletion in a heavily pretreated post-transplant marrow is not a low-toxicity step just because the cells are.
Single site in Seattle. The preferences permit travel, but travel plus lymphodepletion plus cytopenias needs a local backup plan written before she goes.

picks.intervention_label: Sibling donor lymphocyte infusion after debulking, as the lower-intensity alternative to a second graft
picks.rationale: If the fitness workup comes back badly, this keeps curative intent on the table without committing her to a second conditioning regimen. Orti's 46-patient comparison found the univariate survival advantage of a second graft over DLI (p=0.021) did not hold on multivariate analysis once both groups had been debulked, which is thin evidence but it is the only head-to-head in the set. The honest number for her is Schmid's 15% +/- 3% two-year survival for DLI given in aplasia or with active disease, against 56% +/- 10% when given in remission or with a favourable karyotype, and she currently sits on the wrong side of both. That is an argument for cytoreducing before the infusion, not against the infusion.
primary_concerns: GVHD is the toxicity and the mechanism at the same time, and not one of the registry rows grades it, so the risk cannot be quantified for her from this evidence at all.
The trial route is probably shut even where the therapy is not: NCT06529731 caps blasts at 30% and allows a single prior post-transplant line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already spent.
Cell dose and escalation schedule are centre-specific here, so whoever gives it owns the toxicity, and that argues for doing it where her transplant records live.

notes: Rank order follows the sequence I would actually run rather than a standalone preference ordering: document fitness, cytoreduce with the component that has pre-transplant hepatic safety data, graft into a countable remission, then consolidate with the HA-directed product if typing permits. No veto issued in round 1. preferences.json lists no toxicity_vetoes, so the thresholds above are mine and not hers, and I have tried to make them conditional and checkable rather than prohibitive: blasts under 27% or a documented remission before conditioning, a measured ejection fraction before any anthracycline or conditioning regimen, and baseline plus weekly bilirubin/transaminases around any gemtuzumab exposure. Two things I expect to argue in round 2. First, I will veto any rank-1 pick that takes her to conditioning at 85% blasts on the strength of the Iomab-B mechanism, because SIERRA excluded prior HCT and NCT07157514 excludes it again while capping blasts at 20%, so the randomised 17.1% durable-CR result cannot be borrowed for her. Second, rezatapopt: no peer-reviewed effect size exists, PYNNACLE needs RECIST-measurable disease, and Carter's mechanism work shows the drug needs venetoclax to kill, which is the agent she just progressed through. I would also want the CD123 route (pivekimab, 2 dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68) kept away from the pre-conditioning window on hepatic grounds.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) on a cytoreduce-first platform, sibling or alternative donor
picks.rationale: Four independent registries say the same thing about relapse after allo-HCT, which is as close to replication as this question gets: Ruutu 2015 (n=2632, 5-year RFS 15%), Christopeit 2013 (n=179, 2-year OS 37% +/- 6% in the related-donor-first-graft stratum she sits in), Schmid 2012 (n=263) and Schmid 2007 (n=399). All of it is retrospective and none of it adjusts for the obvious confounder, which is that who gets offered a second graft is itself a fitness judgement made by the treating centre. Every favourable number quoted for her is gated on a blast burden she does not have: Schmid 2012's HR 0.53 (0.40-0.72, p<0.001) is for marrow blasts below 27%, and its worst prognostic band is 4% +/- 2% at two years. At 85% blasts she is in that worst band today, so I rank the platform first and treat the debulking question as the thing that actually decides whether any of these estimates apply to her.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I confounding domain is unaddressed in all four registries: selection into a second transplant tracks with fitness, donor availability and centre practice, and no row here adjusts for it
Applicability failure at 85% blasts. The 37% +/- 6% and 32% +/- 7% strata require blasts under 27-35%; quoting them for her as she stands would be an indirectness error, not a rounding error
Non-relapse mortality after a second graft is not tabulated in any of these rows, so the harm side of the estimate is missing entirely
No organ-function or cardiac data in profile.json. Conditioning tolerance is being assumed rather than measured
Orti 2018 (n=46) is too small to support its own equivalence claim between DLI and HCT2; do not read it as evidence the choice does not matter

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF with fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
picks.rationale: NCT04050280 is the best population match among open slots in this dossier (post-allograft relapse explicitly permitted at 60+ days, refractoriness to an intensive regimen required, isolated myeloid sarcoma excluded but marrow disease not), and it has no posted results, so every effect estimate attached to it is imported from somewhere else. The imports do not travel well. ALFA-0701's HR 0.58 (0.43-0.78, p=0.0003) came from untreated de novo AML aged 50-70 in a trial that specifically did not enrol secondary or therapy-related disease, and Hills 2014, the only tier-1a RoB2-low row in the file, puts adverse cytogenetics at OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18), p=0.9, a 2.2% absolute difference at six years. I rank it second on eligibility fit and on the cytoreductive backbone, not on the gemtuzumab component, which is the part with high-quality randomised evidence pointing away from benefit in her karyotype.
primary_concerns: Selective reporting risk on the regimen itself: NCT04050280 is recruiting with no posted results, so the regimen has zero direct evidence in refractory AML

Indirectness on both imports. ALFA-0701 is untreated de novo AML with secondary and therapy-related AML excluded, which is her diagnosis; MyloFrance-1's 26% CR (n=57) is first relapse after chemotherapy, not refractory disease after an allograft, so read it as a ceiling

Hills 2014 adverse-cytogenetics OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18, p=0.9) is a prespecified exploratory stratification in 3325 randomised patients, which is the strongest evidence in this dossier and it is null for her group

CD33 density and rs12459419 are both unmeasured. Laszlo 2019 puts density at r2=0.3124 (P<0.0001) for gemtuzumab cytotoxicity, so it is a partial modifier rather than a gate, and a low reading should not be used to veto anything
ALFA-0701 was open-label with investigator-assessed EFS components (RoB2: some concerns on outcome measurement)

picks.intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley/HighPassBio platform), NCT03326921
picks.rationale: n=9. That is the entire clinical evidence base, 4 of 9 achieved or maintained CR, and the registered primary endpoint of NCT03326921 is manufacturing feasibility and dose-limiting toxicity, so the 44.4% is a descriptive secondary readout and not a pre-specified efficacy result. What separates it from the rest of the HLA-restricted field is that the preclinical work is on the actual clinical construct (Dossa 2018) with independent replication of the target across a 13-TCR panel and 15 HA-1-positive patient samples (Pilunov 2023), plus a protocol that requires prior allo-HCT rather than excluding it. The HA-2 arm should not ride on the same billing: TSC-101 rests on Heemskerk 2003, in vitro, 23 years old, and not the TCR in the clinical product, so treating HA-1 and HA-2 as equivalently evidenced is an error. The evidence is thin and I will not dress it up, but it is the best-supported version of the option this case was submitted to find.
primary_concerns: n=9 in a phase 1 whose registered primary endpoint is feasibility and DLT. Nobody should quote 44.4% as an expected response rate
All three gating genotypes are unretrieved: recipient HLA-A*02:01, recipient HA-1(H) at rs1801284 (A/G or A/A), donor HA-1(H)-negative. Without them the option is a hypothesis, not a plan
No published HA-1 TCR-T data at anything like 85% marrow blasts, and none in extramedullary disease

Antigen-presentation escape is unmeasured. Christopher 2018 and Toffalori 2019 both show non-genomic HLA class II loss after transplant, and Gambacorta 2022 attributes up to 40% of post-transplant relapses to it, which is exactly the failure mode a six-year escape from an HLA-identical sibling graft would predict
Single site, single sponsor, no independent clinical replication of the product

picks.intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123-directed ADC), off-label after the May 2026 BPDCN approval
picks.rationale: Peer-reviewed, in the right disease and the right line, and it reports its own uncertainty honestly: ORR 21% (95% CI 8-40) and composite CR 17% (6-36) in 29 patients at the RP2D (Daver 2024, Lancet Oncology). Response was a secondary endpoint of a dose-finding study whose primary was MTD and RP2D selection, and an interval running from 8% to 40% is not a number to build a plan around. It ranks here mostly on obtainability relative to its competitors: flotetuzumab posted 26.7% CR/CRh in exactly her chemorefractory population (Uy 2021, n=30) and the programme is dead, and lintuzumab-Ac225's 56.6% composite CR comes from a 26-patient dose-escalation with subgroup rates on undisclosed denominators and every trial currently suspended for drug supply. Two dose-limiting veno-occlusive events in 68 patients is the specific thing to weigh in someone being lined up for a second graft.
primary_concerns: ORR was secondary to an MTD/RP2D primary; single-arm, open-label, sponsor-analysed, no OS readout in the R/R AML cohort
95% CI 8-40 on n=29. The point estimate carries almost no information on its own
Veno-occlusive disease before a planned second allograft (2 dose-limiting events in 68), which is the one toxicity that could cost her the transplant
CD123 antigen density is unmeasured, and the 75% frontline BPDCN figure is a different disease and must not be carried across

Cross-check on the alternatives: Vadakekolathu 2020's 47% CR in TP53-abnormal disease is a post-hoc correlative analysis on 15 patients with no CI reported, and should not be cited as a TP53-specific effect size for anything

picks.intervention_label: Sibling donor lymphocyte infusion after cytoreduction
picks.rationale: Schmid 2007 is the only row in this dossier's post-transplant relapse literature carrying a concurrent untreated comparator: 171 given DLI against 228 not, 2-year OS 21% +/- 3% versus 9% +/- 2%, p=0.04, n=399. Confounding by indication is the central problem and the design cannot fix it, since the patients who received DLI are the ones their centres judged well enough to receive it. Her relapse beyond 5 months post-HCT puts her on the favourable side of that variable (p<0.0001), but 85% blasts and an adverse karyotype put her in the 15% +/- 3% stratum rather than the 56% +/- 10% one. Before committing to anything that depends on donor T cells recognising these blasts, measure HLA class II on them.
primary_concerns: Confounding by indication is unadjusted and probably explains a large share of the 21% versus 9% gap
Her stratum is the 15% +/- 3% one (aplasia or active disease), not the 56% +/- 10% one, unless cytoreduction gets her into remission first
NCT06529731 caps blasts at 30% and allows only one prior post-transplant salvage line, which FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax has already spent, so the trial route is shut at present burden
GVHD after DLI is discussed narratively in Schmid 2007 with no per-term adverse-event table, so the harm estimate is not quantified anywhere in this file

notes: Nothing this patient is actually eligible for gets above tier 2b, and the board should say so out loud rather than letting rank order imply otherwise. Explicit non-picks, with the reason. Rezatapopt: no peer-reviewed clinical effect size exists anywhere: the PYNNACLE interim response rates in circulation are sponsor press releases, Schram 2025 is a protocol paper, and Carter 2025 shows reactivated Y220C p53 induces limited or no apoptosis without venetoclax, the drug she has already failed. Note also that NCT06616636 demands a CLIA Y220C call at VAF above 2%, which sits at the detection limit of the very panel that called her TP53-negative, so the assay could decide eligibility instead of the biology. WT1-TCRc4: Chapuis 2019's 100% RFS at median 44 months (n=12) is prophylaxis into patients already in remission, and Mazziotta 2025 gave the same TCR to post-HCT disease (n=15, median OS 242 days, 2-year OS 33%, 3-year 20%) and states it did not clearly improve outcomes. Even that cohort only had 2 of 15 with overt disease. Anyone citing the first figure for this patient is citing the wrong population. Iomab-B: SIERRA is the only phase 3 in the file that hit its registered primary endpoint (durable CR 17.1%, 9.4-27.5, versus 0%, p<0.0001, n=153), and OS did not move at all (HR 0.99, 0.70-1.41, p=0.96). Prior allo-HCT was an exclusion, the FDA declined the filing and demanded an OS study, and both current protocols exclude her. High design tier, no support for use here. 211At-BC8-B10: the entire mechanism rests on Orozco 2013, a syngeneic mouse transplant with a murine anti-CD45, which models neither allogeneic immunology nor the human antibody; no human efficacy is published, and there is no primary preclinical paper at all for the 131I conjugate. Adult CD33 CAR-T: Wang 2015, n=1, progressed at 9 weeks. CBX-250, VIP943, BMS-986497 and GLIDE have no published clinical evidence of any kind. One methodological correction for whoever writes the CD33 section: Laszlo 2019 gives r2=0.3124 (P<0.0001) for CD33 density against gemtuzumab cytotoxicity and r2=0.0136 (P=0.45) against the T-cell-engager format, so density is roughly a third of the variance for an ADC and none of it for redirected T cells. A low density result argues against the ADC and says nothing about the engager or the TCR-T options.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF + fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin), NCT04050280
picks.rationale: Nothing else I want for her works until the marrow comes down off 85%, and this is the one strong-fit trial that names relapse after allogeneic transplant as eligible rather than disqualifying (nct:NCT04050280). The upside I am buying is the CLAG-M backbone with a CD33 payload on top of it: composite CR 56.6%, 50% in the TP53-mutated subgroup and 38.5% after prior venetoclax (pmid:39955432). I will not pretend the gemtuzumab part is proven in her karyotype, because Hills found no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18, p=0.9). What makes it worth the risk anyway is that fractionated dosing produced no veno-occlusive disease in the seven patients transplanted afterwards (pmid:17051246), so a response here buys her the graft instead of costing it.
primary_concerns: The 56.6% belongs to CLAG-M plus lintuzumab-Ac225, and that alpha-emitter is unavailable. CLAG-GO itself has no published efficacy in refractory AML at all.

She progressed through FLAG-IDA plus venetoclax. Another nucleoside-analogue backbone is asking cladribine to succeed where fludarabine failed, and cross-resistance is the likeliest single reason this fails.
Entry needs CD33 on at least 20% of blasts; the flow result on file is qualitative and does not establish that. Quantitative antigen density has to be ordered now, not at screening.
Prolonged aplasia in a six-year-old graft could end the transplant plan rather than enable it, and there are no organ-function numbers anywhere in the profile to price that against.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT with sequential cytoreduction into reduced-intensity conditioning (FLAMSA-style; US analogue NCT06928662)
picks.rationale: Only a graft cures her, and the registry stratification puts her on the good side of every factor except one: six years of remission and a sibling first donor, a stratum that ran 37% +/- 6% two-year survival (pmid:23918951). Schmid's score prices the exception honestly, with blasts under 27% carrying HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.40-0.72) for survival (pmid:22167752), which is exactly why rank 1 sits where it does. The aggressive version I will defend is sequential rather than remission-gated: cytoreduction running straight into reduced-intensity conditioning gave CR in 66 of 75 patients, 59 of whom had progressive or refractory disease, with 42% alive at two years (pmid:16110027). Amsacrine is not marketed in the US, so the reachable form of that idea is nct:NCT06928662 or an institutional sequential regimen.
primary_concerns: Non-relapse mortality on a second graft is the tax nobody avoids, and about half of those who do reach CR relapse again (pmid:23918951).
The US sequential protocol asks her to take a FLAG-Ida backbone she has already progressed through. I would substitute the cytoreduction rather than repeat it.
Ruutu's 15% five-year relapse-free survival across 2632 second transplants is the number to quote if anyone starts describing this as a cure with a percentage attached (pmid:26367221).
The thigh sarcoma is not treated by marrow-directed conditioning and will need its own local plan.
No cardiac or renal data documented. A second conditioning decision cannot rest on ECOG 1 alone.

picks.intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T, donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells (Bleakley platform), NCT03326921
picks.rationale: This is the product the case was submitted for, and the only HA-1 protocol written to require the prior allograft rather than exclude it, with no blast ceiling and no performance-status floor (nct:NCT03326921). Four of nine patients achieved or maintained CR, one MRD-negative past 27 months, with no dose-limiting toxicity, no CRS and no ICANS (pmid:38683966). Nine patients is nine patients and I am not going to dress it up; the counterweight I take seriously is that the same class did nothing against active disease in the WT1 TCR-T cohort (pmid:40473616) and Medigene read tumour burden as the limiting factor in their own PRAME phase 1 (pmid:41008812). That is an argument for sequencing it after cytoreduction, not for dropping it, and it is why the A*02:01 retrieval and HA-1 genotyping of both her and the sibling should be moving this week.
primary_concerns: Two gates are shut: A*02:01 has never been retrieved, and neither she nor the donor is genotyped at HA-1. The mismatch also has to run in one direction, recipient HA-1(H)-positive with an HA-1-negative donor.
Collection, manufacture and lymphodepletion take weeks while her peripheral blasts moved from 58% to 82% inside a month.
The 4 of 9 denominator mixes patients whose remission was induced with patients whose remission was maintained. The induction signal in bulk disease is weaker than 44.4% sounds.
Single site in Seattle, and the neighbouring HA-1 protocol written for exactly this population (NCT04464889) was withdrawn without enrolling anyone.
HLA loss on the blasts would silence every A*02:01-restricted option at once and nobody has looked (pmid:19641204).

picks.intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager against CG1/HLA-A*02:01), NCT06994676
picks.rationale: If A*02:01 comes back positive but the HA-1 mismatch runs the wrong way, this is what keeps the HLA-A2 handle alive, because it needs only the allele: recurrence after HSCT is eligible by name and the extramedullary exclusion applies to isolated lesions, which her marrow involvement takes her out of (nct:NCT06994676). The human evidence is zero and I will say that plainly. What I am betting on is preclinical: the engager killed HLA-A2-positive primary AML in vitro and in vivo (pmid:39939820), and the CAR version of the same target left normal marrow haematopoiesis intact (pmid:40437170). There is also a compassionate-use address on this one, so a full slot list is not the end of the conversation.
primary_concerns: No patient has been treated. First-in-human escalation means she could sit at a dose level chosen to be safe rather than active.
Peptide-HLA engagers have no characterised CRS profile in humans yet, and she would be receiving one in a post-transplant marrow.
Enrolment wants white cells under 25,000/uL, which only holds if cytoreduction is already working.
CG1 appears nowhere on her nominated feature list. This pick rides an HLA restriction, not a validated target in her disease.

picks.intervention_label: 211At-BC8-B10 (astatine-211 anti-CD45) targeted conditioning + allogeneic HCT, NCT03670966
picks.rationale: SIERRA proved the principle that matters for a patient nobody can get into remission: durable CR 17.1% (95% CI 9.4-27.5) with antigen-targeted conditioning against 0% (95% CI 0-4.7) on conventional care, all with active disease at randomisation (pmid:39298738). Her first transplant is the sole reason she cannot have that drug, and the astatine-211 anti-CD45 protocol is the one targeted-conditioning route that admits a prior reduced-intensity allograft (nct:NCT03670966). Published human efficacy for it is nil. What exists is a murine dose-response of 123, 101, 61 and 37 days median survival at 24, 20, 12 and 0 microCi (pmid:23471305), and I would rather spend a phone call now on whether a haploidentical relative exists than find out in three months that we needed one.
primary_concerns: No human efficacy data of any kind for 211At-BC8-B10, and NCT02665065 showed overall survival did not separate (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.70-1.41) even where the durable-CR difference was stark.
The protocol wants a haploidentical relative, not the HLA-identical sibling who gave the 2020 graft. If no such relative exists this pick evaporates.
Myeloablative conditioning in 2020 would exclude her, and the profile does not record what she was given.
Circulating blasts must be under 10,000/mm3, which at 82% peripheral blasts means hydroxyurea has to work first.
Alpha-emitter dosimetry plus a second graft in a heavily pretreated marrow is an unquantified cytopenia risk.

notes: What I passed over and why. Tagraxofusp and pivekimab are real CD123 handles but weaker cytoreduction than CLAG-GO for someone who needs the marrow emptied fast: pivekimab single-agent ORR was 21% (95% CI 8-40) at the RP2D, and reversible veno-occlusive disease in a patient heading for a second graft is the wrong trade (pmid:38423051). Rezatapopt I would normally champion on exactly my grounds, an early signal with a clean mechanism, except Carter showed reactivated Y220C p53 needs venetoclax to actually kill (pmid:40608889), and venetoclax is the drug she just failed; if the variant comes back Y220C I would revisit with an MDM2 or XPO1 partner instead. Flotetuzumab's 26.7% CR/CRh in primary induction failure and 47% in TP53-abnormal disease is the most interesting number in this dossier and the drug does not exist any more, which is worth someone recording. MT-401-OTS and the interferon-gamma DLI study are both good ideas locked behind blast ceilings of 10% and 30%, so they become live only if rank 1 works, and that is the honest sequencing argument for putting cytoreduction ahead of the immunotherapy this case was submitted for.

picks.intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF + fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin) on NCT04050280
picks.rationale: NCCN AML v3.2026 puts clinical trial first for relapsed/refractory disease and lists both halves of this regimen separately in the same pathway: cladribine plus cytarabine plus G-CSF sits in the intensive R/R chemotherapy table, and gemtuzumab ozogamicin is the listed CD33-positive option, on-label for R/R CD33+ AML. NCT04050280 is the one strong-fit trial in the dossier and it is recruiting, so the guideline-preferred route and the practical route are the same thing here. What it buys is cytoreduction, which gates everything downstream. I am not counting on the gemtuzumab component to carry the regimen, because the individual-patient meta-analysis found no survival benefit in adverse cytogenetics (OR 0.99, 0.83-1.18, p=0.9).
primary_concerns: The NCCN R/R chemotherapy table was built from patients who had not already relapsed after an allograft. Nothing in that pathway is calibrated to a second-transplant candidate sitting at 85% marrow blasts.

Gemtuzumab's cytogenetic problem is real and specific to her: pmid 25008258 gives OR 0.99 (0.83-1.18, p=0.9) in adverse karyotype, and hers is complex with del(5q), del(7q), MECOM gain and KMT2A amplification.

No published CLAG-GO efficacy exists in refractory AML. The only CLAG-GO paper in the dossier (pmid 41173347) is frontline core-binding-factor disease, a favourable-risk population that says nothing about this one.

Quantitative CD33 density is still unmeasured. The ALFA-0701 central flow reanalysis tied benefit to expression level rather than to a positive-or-negative call, so the qualitative flow result is a weak basis for choosing an ADC.

The right-thigh myeloid sarcoma may not track with the marrow. NCCN treats extramedullary AML systemically and keeps radiotherapy for local salvage, but the guideline text on myeloid sarcoma is thin, mostly FDG-PET/CT at workup.

picks.intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2), sibling or alternative donor, after cytoreduction
picks.rationale: NCCN AML v3.2026 tells you to start the donor search at first relapse and lists targeted therapy or chemotherapy followed by HCT as the R/R route; ELN 2022 (Dohner, Blood 2022;140:1345-1377) recommends allogeneic HCT once cytoreduction is achieved. Neither body writes a separate graded recommendation for a second allograft after post-transplant relapse, so HCT2 rests on registry evidence and transplant-centre judgement rather than a category. The registry stratification has her on both sides at once: sibling donor and a six-year first remission are favourable in the 2632-patient EBMT analysis, and 85% blasts is not. Read against the guideline text, HCT2 is the consolidation step and not the next thing to do.
primary_concerns: Every guideline statement supporting a transplant here attaches to remission or at least to achieved cytoreduction. At 85% marrow blasts she sits outside the population any of them describes.

No NCCN category attaches to a second allograft after post-transplant relapse. The pathway assumes a first transplant, so anyone quoting a category number for HCT2 is quoting something that does not exist.
Organ function, cardiac status and HCT-CI are undocumented, and the guideline transplant recommendations assume a fitness assessment nobody has done yet.
pmid 22167752 is blunt about the sequencing: long-term survival occurred almost only where cytoreduction reached CR before the second graft or DLI.

picks.intervention_label: Sibling donor lymphocyte infusion after cytoreduction
picks.rationale: The EBMT best-practice recommendations on DLI after allogeneic HCT (Practice Harmonisation and Guidelines Committee with the Cellular Therapy and Immunobiology Working Party, Lancet Haematology 2024) are the closest thing to a graded guideline for post-transplant relapse, and they set therapeutic DLI from a matched sibling at a starting dose of 1x10^7 CD3/kg. Her donor is an HLA-identical sibling who already donated, so the logistics are the easy part. The catch is that those recommendations are written for low burden or post-cytoreduction disease: the EBMT registry puts a patient with 85% blasts and adverse cytogenetics in the 15% two-year survival band rather than the 56% one. NCCN AML v3.2026 carries no DLI recommendation at all, which is worth saying out loud rather than letting the silence read as endorsement.
primary_concerns: DLI into 85% blasts is off-guideline. The EBMT recommendation is built for MRD-level or cytoreduced disease, not for florid haematologic relapse.

A relapse six years out looks like graft-versus-leukaemia escape rather than graft loss. Re-infusing the same donor repertoire that already stopped holding the disease is a bet no guideline addresses.
GVHD is the standard trade and preferences.json vetoes nothing, but grade III-IV GVHD would close the door on HCT2 and on any post-transplant cellular consolidation.
pmid 29526774 compares DLI with HCT2 in 46 patients. Reading that as equivalence is more than the study can hold.

picks.intervention_label: HA-1 TCR-T (donor-derived CD4+/CD8+ memory T cells, Bleakley platform) on NCT03326921
picks.rationale: No guideline lists HA-1 TCR-T, and I want that on the record first: not NCCN AML v3.2026, not ELN 2022, not the EBMT DLI recommendations. What is guideline-endorsed is the route. NCCN's R/R pathway names clinical trial as strongly preferred, and high-resolution HLA typing sits in NCCN's own AML workup, so pulling the 2020 allele-level report is guideline-concordant care rather than a research errand. NCT03326921 is recruiting, requires prior allo-HCT instead of excluding it, and sets no blast ceiling, which is unusual enough to justify the trip if the genotypes line up.
primary_concerns: Two gates are shut. HLA-A*02:01 is unretrieved, and neither the patient nor her sibling has been genotyped at HA-1; the trial needs recipient A/G or A/A with a donor who is G/G.
Phase 1 with n=9 in the published report (pmid 38683966). That is feasibility and dose-limiting-toxicity data, not an efficacy estimate anyone should rank on.
HLA loss or downregulation at relapse would leave every A*02:01-restricted approach blind to these blasts, so pair the typing with a surface class I flow read.
It behaves as post-transplant consolidation. It does not answer the 85% blast burden by itself, and treating it as first-line here would invert the sequence.

picks.intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586) + azacitidine on NCT06616636, contingent on a TP53 Y220C call
picks.rationale: For TP53-aberrant AML the honest guideline position is that no standard option performs well: against poor-risk AML with TP53 mutation or del(17p), NCCN AML v3.2026 lists clinical trial and nothing else. NCT06616636 is recruiting and is the trial-shaped answer that recommendation points at, but it screens on a Y220C call above 2% VAF from CLIA-approved local testing, and this case has no variant-level result in either direction. Resolve the 2019-versus-2026 discrepancy first: original variant identity and VAF, p53 IHC, 17p FISH. If the lesion is not Y220C this pick disappears, and the guideline still says trial.
primary_concerns: Y220C status is unknown, so ranking this at all is contingent. A non-Y220C result drops it off the list entirely rather than demoting it.

No efficacy data in AML. pmid 40608889 found wild-type conformation restored in Y220C AML with limited or absent apoptosis unless combined with venetoclax or MDM2/XPO1 inhibition, and she has already progressed through venetoclax.
An azacitidine backbone is slow against 85% blasts in refractory disease, which sits badly against the stated curative intent.
Eprenetapopt is not the fallback. That programme stopped after the randomised phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its primary endpoint.

notes: Guideline version check, since the dossier does not pin one. I verified NCCN AML content against Version 3.2026 (11/24/2025), read through the NCCN Guidelines for Patients, Acute Myeloid Leukemia, 2026 edition, which states the version it translates. The professional PDF sits behind a login and NCCN appears to have posted later 2026 versions, so treat v3.2026 as the floor and re-check before anything moves clinically. The NCCN Guidelines Insights for AML v3.2026 (JNCCN 2026;24(6):222-229, PMID 42297017) is about MRD monitoring and does not touch the R/R pathway. Two things the board should not misread. First, gemtuzumab: NCCN v3.2026 lists it for CD33-positive AML in the relapsed/refractory targeted-therapy guide with no cytogenetic qualifier, but it is absent from the poor-risk intensive induction options while appearing in the favourable and intermediate induction guides. Hills 2014 is why. On-label for her indication does not mean the guideline expects benefit in her karyotype. Second, revumenib: NCCN v3.2026 lists it for AML with KMT2A rearrangement. She has KMT2A amplification, four copies, which is a different lesion. If another persona picks a menin inhibitor on that basis I will dissent on guideline_fit in round 2. On risk assignment she is adverse under ELN 2022 on at least five independent criteria: complex karyotype, del(5q), del(7q), MECOM gain, abn(17p) from the 2019 der(17)t(13;17), and TP53 if the aberration is confirmed. NCCN v3.2026 uses the same poor-risk list. Myeloid sarcoma is thinly covered everywhere: NCCN's extramedullary content is largely FDG-PET/CT at workup and systemic therapy as the treatment, with radiotherapy for local salvage, and there is no graded recommendation to cite for a thigh lesion in refractory post-transplant disease. On ESMO, the current Clinical Practice Guideline for AML is the 2020 Annals of Oncology document, and I am deliberately quoting no MCBS score anywhere in this position, because ESMO-MCBS v1.1 is a solid-tumour scale and has not been validated for haematological malignancies. Anyone reporting an MCBS grade for these interventions is inventing one.
